content.text:
I now have a clear picture from the grep results. Let me present the answer.

h15.

Memo visibility (who may view a memo) is enforced independently on several server surfaces. The distinct enforcement sites:

Single-memo read access (Connect/gRPC API — `GetMemo`, comment/relation reads) via `checkMemoReadAccess`: PUBLIC open, non-PUBLIC requires auth, PRIVATE requires creator — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39

List/query filtering (`ListMemos`) — builds a store visibility filter so anonymous callers get only PUBLIC and authenticated callers get their own memos plus PUBLIC/PROTECTED — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:216 (the same visibility-list logic is duplicated for the stats surface in server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:84)

Raw attachment/file serving (checks the owning memo's visibility before streaming the blob) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:677

RSS feed (restricts to PUBLIC only) — server/router/rss/rss.go:90

Frontend SSR/metadata rendering (restricts to PUBLIC only) — server/router/frontend/frontend.go:150

Real-time SSE event delivery (`SSEClient.canReceive` filters broadcast events by memo visibility and recipient) — server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:135

Additionally, memo-inheriting sub-resources re-enforce the same visibility rule at their own service boundaries: reactions (server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:30,38,83), memo attachments (server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:214,222 and attachment_service.go:445,451), and comments (server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:41).

Note: I have an Explore agent still running to cross-check for any additional sites; the six primary surfaces above are confirmed directly from the source.

## Memo Visibility Enforcement Sites (memos Go backend)

The visibility model uses three levels defined in `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` (lines 16-21): `Public` = "PUBLIC", `Protected` = "PROTECTED" (workspace/logged-in users), `Private` = "PRIVATE" (creator only). Below are the distinct server-side enforcement sites.

### 1. Central single-memo read-access gate: `checkMemoReadAccess`
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, function `checkMemoReadAccess` (lines 39-68).
- Enforces: For a fetched memo, `PUBLIC` is open; anything non-public requires an authenticated user (else `Unauthenticated`); `PRIVATE` requires `memo.CreatorID == user.ID` (else `PermissionDenied`). Also enforces that `Archived` memos are only visible to their creator (lines 44-53).
- This is the shared helper called by `GetMemo` (line 356, and again for the parent memo at line 367) and by the comment listing path (`memo_service_comments.go` line 148). It is the primary per-memo gate for `GetMemo`/`GetMemoByName`-style reads.

### 2. List-level visibility filtering: `ListMemos`
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, function `ListMemos` (lines 218-227).
- Enforces: Anonymous callers get `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC]` only. Authenticated callers listing across all creators get a CEL filter `creator_id == <id> || visibility in ["PUBLIC","PROTECTED"]`; when listing a specific other creator, `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC, PROTECTED]`. This restricts which memos are returned based on current user vs creator.

### 3. Store/SQL-layer visibility filter (all three DB dialects)
- Files: `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go` (lines 96-102), `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo.go` (lines 89-95), `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/memo.go` (lines 104-110).
- Enforces: Translates `FindMemo.VisibilityList` into a SQL `memo.visibility IN (...)` WHERE clause. This is the actual query-layer restriction backing site #2. `FindMemo.VisibilityList` is defined in `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` line 69.

### 4. Comment creation & listing inherit memo visibility
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`.
  - Comment creation gate (lines 33-41): blocks commenting on a `PRIVATE` memo unless caller is the creator or a super user.
  - Comment listing filter (lines 156-161): builds `visibility == "PUBLIC"` for anonymous, or `creator_id == <id> || visibility in ["PUBLIC","PROTECTED"]` for authenticated, applied via `MemoFilter` to `ListMemoRelations`.

### 5. Reaction access inherits memo visibility
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`.
  - List reactions (lines 29-39): non-public memo requires auth; `PRIVATE` requires creator or super user.
  - Upsert reaction (lines 82-84): `PRIVATE` memo requires creator or super user before allowing a reaction.

### 6. Attachment / resource access inherits memo visibility
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go`, function `checkAttachmentAccess` (lines 422-455): linked attachments follow the memo's visibility — `PUBLIC` open, non-public requires auth, `PRIVATE` requires creator or super user; unlinked attachments are creator-only.
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go`, `ListMemoAttachments`-style path (lines 205-223): re-checks the parent memo's visibility (`PUBLIC` open; `PRIVATE` requires creator/super user) before returning a memo's attachments.

### 7. Memo relations (SetMemoRelations / ListMemoRelations)
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go`.
  - `SetMemoRelations` (lines 35-36): only the memo creator or a super user may modify relations.
  - `ListMemoRelations` (lines 107-111): applies `visibility == "PUBLIC"` (anonymous) or `creator_id == <id> || visibility in ["PUBLIC","PROTECTED"]` (authenticated) as a `MemoFilter` so related/referenced memos the caller can't see are filtered out. The filter is compiled into SQL in `/bench/repo/store/db/{sqlite,postgres,mysql}/memo_relation.go` (sqlite lines 80-85).

### 8. File server (raw attachment/blob HTTP endpoint) enforcement
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 674-703).
- Enforces: For serving raw attachment bytes, `PUBLIC` served to anonymous only when `Profile.AllowAnonymous()`; otherwise a valid non-expired `share_token` for that memo grants access; else an authenticated user is required, and `PRIVATE` requires `user.ID == memo.CreatorID` or `RoleAdmin`. This is a separate (Echo/HTTP, non-gRPC) enforcement path.

### 9. Public render surfaces hard-limited to PUBLIC
- RSS feeds: `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go` (lines 90, 141) force `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC]`.
- Frontend sitemap: `/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go` (line 150) forces `VisibilityList = [PUBLIC]`.

### 10. Share link creation/management is creator-gated
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go` (lines 43-44, 92-93, 133-134): creating/listing/deleting a share requires the memo creator or a super user. `GetMemoByShare` (line 153) and `getActiveMemoShare` (line 199) provide the token-based bypass path (checked against expiry) that the fileserver at #8 also honors.

Notes:
- `isSuperUser(user)` is the admin/host override used consistently across sites #1, #4-#7, #10.
- The two conceptually central, always-applied enforcement points are `checkMemoReadAccess` (single-memo, site #1) and the `ListMemos` + store `VisibilityList` pair (list-level, sites #2/#3). Everything else (comments, reactions, attachments, relations, fileserver) inherits from these same rules at its own access point.</result>
